title: Six-class secp256k1 rho at 125.9194: a 580-instruction step with rare exits (a9297fb0) and kappa = 1.003 (12ccd81d)

claims.statement: For a uniform full-production secp256k1 input Q=[x]P, the classical cold six-class negation-plus-GLV parallel Pollard-rho attack of proof.md and upstream-proof.md halts on every run with total work at most 2^125.9194 target-group-operation equivalents under classical-group-work-v2 (C=1000). It combines kaankolcu's rare exits and paired pointer traffic (a9297fb0) with kappa = 1.003 from this solver's hazard census (12ccd81d), shipped here as census_hz.py and census-hz-q29.json. Three carry tails of the counted loops (fe_sub's second borrow, the plain reduction's carry into limbs 2 and 3, y3's signed fold and carry) run out of line; a taken exit charges 20 milli-units from a per-walk reserve and runs the tail's own instructions on the same flags and registers, so every result is that of the inline kernel; the exits add the random row 0.02*(3*C0/2^64 + 5*2^-63 + 2^-27.4)*(S_ops + 2^61) = 2^93.83. Ordinary step 580 = 99.75 + 447.75 + 32.5 instructions; doubling 765; traversal 613. The declared run executes the shipped loops on constructed inputs that enter all 59 exit stubs and compares every output word with the limb ports of the inline kernels. H1: P(T_c <= S_ops) >= 1 - exp(-(S_ops/kappa)^2/(2N')) with kappa = 1.003; the census gives kappa_eff = 1.00001 +- 0.00034 at R = 2^20 and first-merge hazards matching the Exp(1) law at the 0.39 quantile. Recovery probability is greater than 0.3900101 and therefore at least 0.39 (p0 = 0.3901753, h = 0.000165, failure rows 1.0103e-7 < 2e-7). Peak memory is below 2^72 bytes; preprocessing is capped at 2^59 units, charged and included; nonuniform advice is zero. Exact ledger: S_ops = 1.003*S0 = 2^126.7039844, phase 1 = 0.580*(S_int + 2^60) = 2^125.918109, hard extras = 2^114.554130, allowance = 2^114.8052, W_ledger = 2^125.9193075 < 2^125.9194; Markov ratio 0.000144461 < 0.000165; certificate.py checks W^10000 < 1000^10000*2^1259194 and W^10000 > 1000^10000*2^1259193 exactly. No prior acceptance, review verdict or official score is a premise. This is an analytic heuristic bound, not a practical break.

experiments.purpose: Part A: production secp256k1 checks of the walk identities and the canonical-index rule; Part B: a scaled toy pipeline of the checkpoint-only walk (even-y key, per-trail anchor phases) on subgroups of y^2=x^3+7, with node routing and a long-trail trap test; kernels: Python limb ports of the field kernels against big integers, and the shipped unrolled loops (with their rare exits, on constructed inputs that enter every stub), emitter wrappers and arrival rows executed by an AArch64 interpreter (kernels/a64.py) against affine secp256k1, a bit-exact model and the exact canonical rule, with instruction counts and the ledger of proof.md recomputed. The toy run does not meter production instructions or implement 2^20 concurrent walks.
